title: Chwalinska’s breakout season reaches new heights with a WTA 1000 title in Wuhan
description: Maja Chwalinska completed another breakthrough week in Wuhan, rallying from a set down to defeat Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 and capture her first WTA title. The Pole became just the fourth player since 2009 to win her maiden WTA title at the WTA 1000 level.

body:
It hadn't always been smooth sailing for Maja Chwalinska since her breakthrough at Roland Garros earlier this year, but the 25-year-old proved her run to the final in Paris was no fluke with another remarkable week in Wuhan, capturing her first career title. 

The No. 16 seed rallied from a set and a break down and faced a critical juncture at 4-all in the second set before forcing a decider. She then won the final four games -- saving three break points while serving for the match -- to defeat World No. 170 Sonay Kartal 2-6, 6-4, 6-2 in 2 hours, 43 minutes and lift the 2026 Dongfeng · Voyah Wuhan Open trophy.

Chwalinska is the fourth player on the WTA Tour Driven by Mercedes-Benz since the format's introduction in 2009 to win her first title at the WTA 1000 level, joining Naomi Osaka (Indian Wells 2018), Bianca Andreescu (Indian Wells 2019) and Victoria Mboko (Montreal 2025).

She is also the fourth player to win a maiden WTA 1000 title this season, following Karolina Muchova (Doha), Marta Kostyuk (Madrid) and Zheng Qinwen (Beijing). 

The title carried added significance. Chwalinska became the first left-hander to win a WTA 1000 title since Petra Kvitova in Miami in 2023 and just the third Polish player to claim a WTA 1000 title, after Agnieszka Radwanska and Iga Swiatek. She defeated Swiatek in the semifinals en route to the championship.
